questions.prompt: Which statement about constructors is correct?
options: A constructor must always have a return type of void.
A constructor is called automatically when an object is created.
A constructor must have the same name as the class in lowercase.
A constructor can return a value using the return statement.
questions.explanation: A constructor is a special method that runs automatically when an instance of a class is created. It has no return type—not even void—and its name must match the class name exactly with the same casing.

Which statement about static constructors is true?
options: A static constructor can have parameters.
A static constructor is called every time an object is created.
A static constructor is called once per type, before any instance is created or static members are accessed.
A static constructor must be public.
questions.explanation: A static constructor runs exactly once per type, automatically, before the type's first use—whether that is creating an instance, accessing a static field, or invoking a static method. It takes no parameters and has no access modifiers.
